commits.message: expectLinearTime's own tests pin that a stalled larger run cannot fail linear work, and the floor comment names only the sizes that measure growth (rich-unfiled-791c.acoa)

expectLinearTime's own tests run their smaller size about three times over the floor on GitHub's runner (rich-unfiled-791c.acoa)

The unloaded run in 'passes linear work when the machine turns busy partway
through' took ~4.9 ms on GitHub's runner against FLOOR_MS = 5 (CI run
39060726759). The quadratic cases sat at ~7 ms, the same failure one faster
runner away. The stall is now four times the run it delays, so the stalled
pair's ratio no longer depends on the size.

Markdown reads each text's backtick runs once instead of rescanning for every unclosed opener (rich-unfiled-791c.lbtu) (#453)

* Markdown reads each text's backtick runs once instead of rescanning for every unclosed opener (rich-unfiled-791c.lbtu)

inlineAt's code case compiled a RegExp per backtick run and scanned to the
end of the text for a closer of that length, so a paragraph of openers no
run closes took time quadratic in its length: `\``x ` repeated 32,000 times
took 4.5 s. InlineState (formerly LinkLabels — it now holds more of
markdown-it's inline state than the label scan) indexes each text's whole
runs by length once, and an opener looks up the first run of its length
after it: 15 ms for the same input.

A differential run of 200,000 random inputs (116,673 with code spans,
escaped partial openers and link labels among them) against the previous
reader found no difference in output.

* Markdown indexes a block's backtick runs once and shares them with every link label cut from it (rich-unfiled-791c.lbtu)

Keying the index by text built a fresh one for each link's sliced label,
so a paragraph of [`a`](u) links took quadratic time and memory. A label
is cut at its ']', never inside a run, so the block's runs bound by the
label's length are the label's runs.
